title: Expenses revision, format v1
description: The plaintext of one revision of an Expenses record (ADR 0108 decisions 3-5, docs/apps/expenses.md): an expense, a refund, a transfer or a participant, a deletion of one of them, or a participant's erasure. Compact UTF-8 JSON, padded to the smallest size class that carries it (`u32be(len) || bytes || zeros` to 512, 2048, 8192 or 16384 bytes, `@veyq/crypto`'s `padToClass`) and sealed under the revision's own K_rev with the `expense-entry` field seal, bound to (scope, Pot node, entry id, revision); K_rev is wrapped under the Pot's key by `expense-entry-key` (contracts/crypto/vectors/v1.json). The server sees none of it. Readers ignore unknown fields: a field added later under `v: 1` is additive, and a change an older reader would misread is `v: 2`. The `amounts` split mode joined after the first revisions were written and is not additive (a reader that predates it refuses the split's mode); it stays `v: 1` because no release exists yet (scripts/applied_migrations.sha256's `release:` is `none`), so no reader of the earlier v1 is in anyone's hands, and every revision written before it reads unchanged. Arithmetic (part of the version, ADR 0108 decision 9): amounts are integers in the minor unit of their currency (`minorUnits` digits, ISO 4217); a `rate` is a decimal string and every computation is exact. Every allocation below is the largest-remainder rule: an integer total T by weights w, each person's exact `T * w / sum(w)` rounded down, the units left over handed one each to the largest cut-off remainders, ties by the order given. An entry's `amount` is the sum of its payers' (a refund: receivers') amounts. Its total converts once into the Pot's base currency, `round_half_away_from_zero(amount * rate * 10^(baseMinorUnits - minorUnits))`. That base total is allocated to the payers (receivers) by their amounts, in join order; and to the entry's parts — each item in its order, then the rest `amount - sum(items)` when it is above zero — by their amounts in the entry's currency, in that order (where the currency is the base, every part gets exactly its own amount). Each part's base amount is then allocated among the people of its split, in join order, by 1 each (`equal`), their shares (`shares`), their basis points (`percent`) or their amounts in the entry's currency (`amounts`: the part's base amount allocated by those amounts as weights, so where the currency is the base every person gets exactly their amount); a person's share of the entry is the sum of their parts. Join order is the participants' `joined`, then their id. A revision whose amounts do not add up (payers' or receivers' amounts not summing to `amount`, items above it, a rest above zero with no split, percents not summing to 10000, the amounts of a split not summing to the amount of the part it splits — an item's amount, or the rest while it is above zero (a rest split sealed at a zero rest splits nothing and is held to no sum) —, a person named twice among the payers or receivers or within one split) is invalid: a reader counts it nowhere and shows it as invalid. contracts/expenses/v1-vectors.json pins every rule with worked cases.

v.description: The format version (ADR 0079 decision 7); the rounding rule above is part of it.

heads.description: The Pot's heads as this revision's writer read them (ADR 0108 decision 5): every revision of the Pot that no other revision it read names. A reader checks that each named revision is present and matches its digest; one missing is covered only by an erasure of its own record. Empty for the first revision of an empty Pot. A writer that read more than 64 heads names the 64 oldest by the time the server stored them; the next write names the rest.

uuid.description: A canonical lowercase UUID, minted by the client (ADR 0072 decision 3).

digest.description: SHA-256 of that revision's sealed body exactly as the server serves it (the decoded `expense-entry` envelope), 32 bytes in base64url without padding. A re-key re-wraps K_rev and leaves the body, so no digest moves.

minor.description: An amount in the minor unit of its currency, a safe integer so every JSON reader reads it exactly.

minorUnits.description: The currency's minor-unit digits as the writer counted them (ISO 4217: the yen 0, the euro 2, the dinar 3). Sealed with the amounts, so no reader's currency table can move them.

rate.description: What one major unit of the entry's currency is worth in major units of the Pot's base currency, as a decimal string greater than zero (`1` where the currency is the base). Fetched or typed (ADR 0108 decision 8); never moved by a later table.

date.description: The day the money moved, `YYYY-MM-DD`, as the writer entered it (no time zone).

category.description: One of the default categories, whose ids the client translates (docs/apps/expenses.md § The Pot), or the id of one of the Pot's own, named in its sealed meta.

receipts.description: The receipts this revision holds, by receipt id (ADR 0108 decision 7). A receipt no revision holds any more is erased after the trash retention. Empty until receipts exist.

split.description: Who one part of an entry (an item, or the rest) is for, and by which weights: each person 1 (`equal`), their shares (`shares`), their percent in basis points, 1 to 10000 summing to exactly 10000 = 100.00 % (`percent`), or a fixed amount each in the entry's currency, summing to exactly the part's amount (`amounts`). A sum other than 10000, or other than the part's amount, makes the entry invalid — rules the schema cannot state.

amount.description: In the entry's currency; a split's amounts sum to the amount of the part it splits.

allocation.description: Who the amount is for (docs/apps/expenses.md § Entries): a list of items, each an exact amount with its own split, and the rest — `amount - sum(items)` — with a split of its own. An entry with no items is all rest (the everyday case: one total, split among everyone). `rest` is required while the rest is above zero and ignored when it is zero (a writer leaves it out then); items above `amount` make the entry invalid.

expense.description: Money one or more payers paid for the beneficiaries.

payers.description: Who paid how much, in the entry's currency; `amount` is their sum (the editor derives it).

refund.description: Money one or more receivers received for the beneficiaries (a credit for a delayed flight): an expense with the signs turned, counted against its category.

receivers.description: Who received how much, in the entry's currency; `amount` is their sum (the editor derives it).

refunds.description: The expense this refunds, when the writer named one. Informational: it moves no amount.

transfer.description: Money one participant gave another (settling up). Not a cost: it has no category.

participant.description: A person of the Pot (ADR 0108 decision 2): a name, or a member of the space (`member`). Entries name it by the record's entry id. A participant never changes kind: its record's first revision decides whether it is a member, and which, for the record's life — a reader ignores a later revision's `member` that differs from the first's, and a writer carries the first's unchanged.

name.description: The name the Pot shows. For a member, their display name when they were added, sealed with their id: what a reader without the space's member directory (a link guest) shows; a member's client shows the current one.

member.description: Added after the first records were written, additive under `v: 1`: a reader that predates it ignores it and reads the record as its `name`. Present: the participant is this member of the space. An erased or departed account leaves it standing, shown as a former member.

userId.description: The member's user id, as the space's member list serves it.

active.description: False once a member deactivated it: entries keep the name; new entries and the overviews no longer offer it.

joined.description: When the participant was added, in milliseconds since the epoch by its first writer's clock, carried unchanged by every later revision of the record: with the record id it is the join order the rounding and the settle-up break ties by.

deleted.description: An expense, refund or transfer deleted: it leaves the list and the balances and stays restorable (a later revision carrying its content again). The append marks it as a tombstone to the server.

erasure.description: A participant deleted or removed by a member (ADR 0108 decision 3): written through the member-only erasure, after which the server holds no earlier revision of the record. It keeps the join order and no name.
